literal: Having studied, and having understood, and having expounded to others, oneself not self-controlled, than that fool, greater fools there are none.
translation: There are no greater fools than those who, despite having studied, understood, and taught others, do not practice self-control themselves.
modern: நூல்களைப் படித்து, அவற்றின் பொருளை உணர்ந்து, பிறருக்கும் எடுத்துச் சொல்லியும், தான் அதன்படி அடங்கி நடக்காத பேதையை விடப் பெரிய பேதையர் யாரும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet defines the ultimate form of foolishness. A person might read many books, grasp their deep meanings, and even teach these values to others. However, if they fail to control their own desires and actions according to that knowledge, their learning is entirely useless. The poet emphasizes that there is no greater fool than someone who possesses knowledge but fails to live by it.
